nodes.label:
A conversational builder starts alone and proposes candidate capabilities.
The host waits for human admission until an approved configuration change
assigns admission authority. A reviewer is added only by an approved change. PAE is the assembled
behavior of these parts. It introduces no phantom runtime control parts.
Runtime evidence remains in the host store. The host interprets the native
bounded action-flow subset and the configured policy and mandates;
definitions alone do not establish an admitted capability or execution.

The builder's ordinary reply branch produces response text.
Reply and invocation request are alternative conversational choices,
not ordered phases of candidate promotion. Native allocation
identifies the performer used by the bounded native-flow interpreter;
it does not establish observed execution.

The builder requests invocation. The host checks the active
capability, unchanged digest and user-supplied HTTPS URL before
executing it. This action does not claim tool execution by builder.

Bounded software operator. It proposes candidates and requests
active catalog invocations. An approved mandate revision can admit
its tested candidates; activation remains a host responsibility.

A separately configured operator reviews the exact tested digest
and may admit that reviewed candidate when its mandate permits it.
It is not an authenticated human approver; activation stays in host.

Awaiting human admission survives host restart. It does not
inherit the interrupted-stage restart behavior of testing/reviewing.

Each occurrence owns its runtime name, digest, candidateId and
status attributes. Source, tests and review evidence remain in the
host store. proposed, testing, reviewing, awaiting-admission, refused,
activating, active and failed describe host state; declaration alone
is not activation.

The host tests the exact candidate in an isolated process.
This is a candidate test sandbox, not a persistent operator workspace.

Host admission gate. Checks passing tests, current admission
authority, exact digest, unchanged bytes, current catalog revision and
unused active name. A pending human decision cannot activate a tool.

Owns candidates and executes admitted activation. After the model
write is verified, the host exposes the active digest for invocation.
The later run of a tool is separate from this promotion behavior.

Host admission uses the current approved system configuration.
Human UI consent is not an authenticated approver receipt.

Native responsibilities for the evolving system. The host controls
tests, pending admission, refusal and activation. These declarations
are configuration, not an observed execution trace.

APE 1.3 - Conversational Case Management.
Native description of a bounded conversational case.
The TypeScript host retains the session, reads its state, controls effects
and presents outcomes to the same builder. The host interprets the supported
native action occurrences, successions and decision guards; named action
definitions select implemented primitive mechanisms. This is a bounded
executable subset, not a complete SysML interpreter. Waiting suspends this
open case; it is not closure.
No verified closure or accepted-handoff mechanism exists in this slice.

The host session identifies the continuing case. Its stored
messages, candidates, configuration and outcomes form the case record.

Host-validated builder decision: reply, invoke_tool, invoke_behavior, propose_tool,
propose_mandate_change or propose_agent_creation. This field describes
those existing choices; it adds no tool or permission.

Success, reported execution failure or refusal is retained for
the next choice. Admission alone never establishes execution success.

A tested tool awaiting admission or a governance change proposal
yields control for an explicit human command. A completed/refused tool
promotion instead supplies feedback for another bounded choice.

A new user message or an explicit admission/refusal command
resumes the stored session under its current approved configuration.

Suspension until another permitted input or admission command.
The model does not assert that the host has formally closed a case.

The host validates the selected active tool, exact digest, target
URL and network scope under the current approved mandate, or the exact
source-owned behavior exposure, caller, typed input and source version.

The host runner attempts the admitted catalog or modeled behavior invocation.
Reported success and failure both continue through observation.

Dispatches the already chosen tool or governance proposal to the
existing host path. Tool construction uses CapabilityPromotion in the
configured system. Governance proposals await a separate human command.
This action neither grants rights nor creates an extra promotion part.

Host feedback retains the reported result or refusal in the same
session before the builder receives its next decision context.

Neutral structural primitives. These definitions carry values and
communication contracts; they do not create runtime control actors.

Fixed host configuration for a software-operator role. The holder
binding identifies the concrete operator. This item does not implement
a grant/revocation registry or authenticate a delegating operator.
evidenceLevel configured records the source level, not execution proof.
grantingOperator unknown means no authenticated grantor is established.

The builder requests a capability by its host catalog identity.
This request is not evidence that the host executed the tool.

Digest of the exact name, description, kind and source bytes
proposed by the builder. Identity remains stable through promotion.
This identifies a candidate and its basis; it is not the canonical
promotion contract governing proofs, admission and closure.

Test evidence belongs to the candidate passed to the test sandbox.
The host retains that association; its TestReport has no digest field.

approved represents the host review verdict "approve".
A review expresses an advisory judgment; it grants no catalog authority
and is not an authenticated-approver receipt.

The admission gate's decision about promotion of these exact bytes.
This is distinct from the independent review decision. It represents
the logical host branch, not an additional persisted verdict record.

Policy consumed from the selected native model by the host's bounded
action-flow interpreter. Native successions and guards determine order;
named action definitions select the standalone primitive-handler registry
of implemented mechanisms. Unknown primitives fail closed. This
package does not claim support for the complete SysML execution language.
Revision permissions permit proposals subject to approved configuration
changes. They do not immediately widen the active mandate or network scope.

Approved capability contract source. Criteria are newline-separated
text. Implemented host test mechanisms remain selected by the supported
kind and module identity; a candidate does not invent its contract.

Candidate promotion lifecycle specified from SystemRuntime.build,
stage and initialize in src/application/system-runtime.ts. The host owns
execution and retained status; this state machine is a native design
description, not proof that a transition occurred in a live session.

AdmissionAccepted means the host has checked passing tests,
approval for the exact digest, unchanged candidate bytes, the current
base catalog revision and an unused active name. ActivationCompleted
follows verified model write and host catalog update. A digest/base/
name mismatch or an exception ends the pending attempt as failed.
Restart never promotes a pending candidate. active, refused and
failed have no outgoing promotion transition; a correction creates
a new candidate. Later invocation does not change this lifecycle.

Mission bornée de démonstration : rechercher des signaux publics de
prestation ou de formation IA pour Casys. Ce texte cadre le travail des
opérateurs ; il ne prétend pas qu’une veille réelle a déjà été exécutée.
Les deux items ci-dessous restent dans le même fichier pour éprouver
deux propositions concurrentes sur des éléments natifs distincts.

APE 4.1 Operator Identity & Mandate: bounded source-editing delegation.
Proposals remain subject to 2.1 Proposal–Admission–Execution Separation.
This declaration configures permissions; it is not execution evidence.

Explicit source-admitted editing bounds for the bound holder and
current mandate. Operations and file/qualified-root pairs are canonical
JSON arrays. Definitions alone grant no editing authority.

APE 2.1 - Proposal–Admission–Execution Separation, with
APE 2.2 - Fail-Closed Admission. Bounded PAE assembly for candidate
promotion. PAE abbreviates proposal, admission and execution. Proposing,
judging and admitting are separate actions allocated to the concrete
system's existing parts. The assembly is behavior, not an extra runtime
part. Here execution means activating the admitted candidate; a later
invocation of that capability is a separate operation.
Related use cases: Task Automation and Change Control. These are
compositions, not patterns 3.1 Decision-to-Effect Traceability or
3.2 Instance-Bound Controls. This bounded slice does not establish full
composition conformance, authenticated approval, rollback or closure.
Historical source identity 7: composition-7-agent-built-deterministic-capability.mjs.
Historical source identity 8: composition-8-sandboxed-candidate-construction-with-controlled-promotion.mjs.
These filenames identify sources, not the public titles or chapter numbers.

Executes the admitted catalog change. The host first writes and
verifies the active state through the native-model adapter, then marks
this candidate active
and advances the host catalog revision. Those adapter integrity checks
are implementation details inside activation, not PAE phases.
An exception leaves the candidate failed and unavailable.

Leaves the candidate outside the active catalog and returns the
refusal to the builder. Integrity exceptions instead end the attempt
as failed; they never grant permission or trigger activation.

Native control flow specifies the successful completion and
refusal routes. Test failure skips review; review refusal skips
admission. Admission alone authorizes activation. The constraints
state obligations; the TypeScript host interprets the supported native
model constructs. Digest
mismatch, stale base, duplicate active name and write failures abort
the host attempt as failed, with no activation.

Bounded design requirements from SystemRuntime.build and runTurn in
src/application/system-runtime.ts. Satisfaction links assign design
responsibilities; they are neither test results nor execution evidence.
Runtime behavior and exact checks are governed by that host source.

Activation requires approval for the same candidate digest.
The host rejects a review with a mismatched digest and rechecks the
current draft digest before entering activation.

A later invocation resolves an active candidate by identifier
and rechecks its digest. Proposal, review or admission alone does
not make a candidate callable. These values describe the host gate;
they are not inferred execution evidence from the diagram.

A refused or failed candidate remains outside the active
catalog. Pending candidates become failed on restart. A correction
is a new proposal, not automatic promotion of the old candidate.

Generic technical entries into modeled operator runtimes and their
artifact catalogs. A performed occurrence must be allocated to the exact
operator or catalog in its owning ConversationSystem. BehaviorAccess
separately fixes every authorized caller. These definitions grant no
admission, network scope or access to another conversation.

The host correlates one admitted request with one operator's
own modeled flow. It transmits this request, never peer history.

Reuse exact published bytes as a local proposal. Local tests,
mandate, admission and activation remain mandatory.

Read metadata of exact active artifacts in the same modeled
system. Neither source code nor conversations nor rights are copied.

A closed plan describes a complete dependency graph before dispatch.
Each task references an exact BehaviorAccess already exposed to its caller.
The host admits every task input before the first invocation, correlates
each receipt, and preserves interrupted or waiting work for explicit resume.
tasksJson is the bounded transport representation of task records, not
permission to address arbitrary operators or inspect their histories.
This mechanism schedules admitted work dependencies; it is not a calendar.
